lead: The Nou Barris closest to the centre, with an old core more than five centuries old and a high street of its own.
text: It is the southernmost neighbourhood in Nou Barris and was developed before the others. Its old core brings together the church of Santa Eulàlia de Vilapicina, Ca n'Artés, an inn from the 15th and 16th centuries, and Can Basté, an 18th-century farmhouse (masia). After the war, the grounds of the Torre Llobeta, owned by the army, were allocated to social housing: an estate of eleven blocks occupied between 1952 and 1955. In the old Borbó bus depots there is a large block of public facilities with a library, a sports centre, a senior citizens' centre and a health centre.

That whole area now forms a community with a personality of its own. Carrer de Cartellà-Costa i Cuixart works as its high street, and Plaça de Virrey Amat as its most central meeting point. The manor house of the Torre Llobeta has been a civic centre since 1983. At 3,569 €/m², its sale price is the highest in Nou Barris. If you are selling, the average sale price is 21% above the Nou Barris average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 286,000 € on average, and this is one of the most expensive neighbourhoods in Nou Barris (1st of 13 by price). If you are investing, the average rent (888 €/month) is 12% above the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: A social housing estate of blocks from the 1950s and flats from different periods.
places: Església de Santa Eulàlia de Vilapicina
